_doc: ledger 0097 round 5, owed item 3: the north loop's 42 m of carried edges (north_loop.json's rows: R row s 0-19, the fork's mouth; R 988-1001 and L 996-1001, the merge's mouth; L 254-260), the asphalt's edge read off the 2018 lidar's INTENSITY. off_osm_m is the rows' own convention (metres outward off OSM's line at the row's s); off_osm_naip_def_m takes off the registration below (c and the shift), giving what NAIP's reader would have read: the value a carried row would take. o_past_built_edge_m is past the north loop's built lane edge (source/full/connectors.full.json).

source.lidar: USGS 3DEP CO_Eastern_B3_2018 lidar (public domain), its EPT: https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/usgs-lidar-public/CO_Eastern_B3_2018/ept.json
source.returns: every class but noise (7, 18); one flight line over all five spots: [1141]
source.frame: the track frame: E, N metres about data/centerline.local.json's origin, lon / lat through scripts.geometry.projection._meters_per_degree (round 4's mapping); 3857 -> lon / lat by pyproj
source.lines: the West lap as built (data/centerline.local.json + widths); the north loop's own line (source/full/connectors.full.json + widths: 'own s', the s of round 4's kerbs and stripes); OSM's line as measure_north.py builds it ('row s', north_loop.json's rows, whose left_m / right_m are metres off it)
source.script: hp_r5_lidar.py beside this file (plan / fetch / extract / measure)

params._doc: every one [invented] reader tuning; the returns are the measurement

registration._doc: the lidar's asphalt edge against NAIP's own on every north-loop row both read in the five spots (the north loop's kerb runs and the two stripes left out): d = lidar - NAIP, metres outward off OSM's line, fitted d = c + (shift_E, shift_N) . n_out. c is the readers' difference: the lidar's first bright return is the INNER side of the first paint (the white edge line is paint, retro-reflective at the scanner's 1064 nm), NAIP's edge is the line's outer side + the photo's line-to-edge offset (round 4: 0.3 m left, 0.4 m right). The shift is the 2018 lidar against the 2023 photo.

l254_260._doc: L rows 240-272, the carried 254-260 inside them; NAIP's rows beside them read on the same faint edge line (round 4's second read)
l254_260.beyond: past the asphalt a grey strip (intensity ~2,200-2,900, between asphalt ~800 and the prairie ~5,300) runs 3-3.5 m before the prairie: round 4's 'verge greying into the prairie'; not asphalt by the lidar
